title: Per-arena themes — 5 visual themes (warehouse / factory / dock / lab / bunker) via theme JSON + palette + Wang family mapping
intent: Per `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §9.2`: each arena should ship with a THEME — a small JSON declaring palette + Wang family choices that change the arena's identity without touching geometry. 5 starter themes: warehouse (industrial steel + concrete), factory (red brick + iron girders), dock (weathered wood + rope), lab (clean white + blue accents), bunker (drab grey + olive). Each theme = ~10 hex colors + 1 line per Wang family. Arenas pick their theme via scene field; multiplayer worlds pick per-world. Closes the 'every arena looks the same colour-wise' gap that becomes visible once lighting + Wang autotile + per-tile variety ship. Cheap to implement (data-only), high visual return (transforms identical geometry into distinct identities).
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §9.2` (5 themes explicitly listed but never filed as a story). Pairs with the entire visual-fidelity batch: themes only feel different when there's enough render surface (multi-light + per-tile variety + Wang autotile) to differentiate them. After 028-001/002/003/004 ship, themes become the multiplicative finishing touch. ~10 hex codes per theme = trivial implementation; the work is in picking distinct, readable palettes per theme + wiring them into Wang family registration.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: 028-001 (lighting/shadow), 028-002 (Wang autotile), 028-003 (tile variants), 028-004 (integration showcase). Best ships AFTER these — themes need the underlying visual surface to differentiate. Could partially ship with just 028-003 if dev wants early visual win.
READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §9.2` (5-theme list with hex hints) + `gdd.md` arena variant section.
ArenaTheme component (singleton on the kaboom.game-state entity, or attached to scene metadata):
Each theme is a static registered config — projects don't author themes per-arena, they CHOOSE from the registered 5.
floorPaletteFamilyOrder: ['floor', 'dirt', 'stone'] (preferred FloorTerrain families when not author-specified)
hardBlockPalette: { primary: #6e5040, accent: #d04020 } (iron with hot-pipe red)
accentEmissive: #ff4444 (warm red for accents — explicit deviation from default cyan in this theme)
hardBlockPalette: { primary: #d8dade, accent: #4080ff } (white panel + blue accent)
softBlockPalette: { primary: #c4c8d0, accent: #5090ff } (white crate + blue stripe)
Scene file: 'themeKey' field on scene-load. Default 'warehouse' if absent.

ArenaThemeApplySystem (project-side): on scene-load reads themeKey + writes palette into the per-bomber + per-tile palette resolvers. Also writes the directional light tint into the existing light setup from 028-001.
WangTileFamilyRegistry (engine module from 028-002): registers same family keys per theme (e.g. floor family has its colours tinted by the theme).
MULTIPLAYER: worldConfig gains `theme: ArenaTheme.key`. Server sends in joinWorld; clients render their own visuals from the theme table (theme tables are client-bundled, identical across tabs).
wide arena → warehouse (same theme, larger floor space)
Per scene file → can override with their own themeKey.
Procbomber-bench gains a 'Theme' dropdown (5 options) — bench preview switches palette + lighting + family selections live. Useful for tuning theme palettes by eye.
PROCBOMBER PALETTE FAMILY OVERRIDES (interaction with character recipes from S102):
Bomber palette families (sky/ember/mint/plum/sand/jade/rose/slate) STAY arena-theme-independent. Bombers maintain identity across themes — their colour is THEIRS not the arena's.

Optional polish (not v1): a few bomber palette families read SLIGHTLY differently in lab theme (higher ambient brightness) vs bunker (lower ambient). Acceptable side-effect of the lighting tint; not a per-theme palette override.
All 5 themes registered + lookupable by key.
ArenaThemeApplySystem on theme=warehouse → directional light tint applied + floor palette applied.
Theme change at runtime (debug probe) → scene re-tints within 1 frame.
Default fallback to 'warehouse' if scene has no themeKey.
Each theme's hex values are valid + within visual-style.md palette discipline (no pure white, no pure black per §5.4 forbidden palettes).

Load each of the 6 arena variants with their default theme assignment → 5 visibly distinct atmospheres (corridor / plaza / cross / pit map to 4 different themes; default + wide share warehouse but that's intentional for the introductory experience).
Override default → lab theme on default arena → arena reads clean+bright. Override to bunker → reads dim+claustrophobic.
visual-style.md §9.2 — mark themes 'shipped 2026-05-XX' once this lands. Update theme hex codes from 'tentative' to 'ratified'.
gdd.md World section + arena variants table — note that each arena variant has a default theme.
`?theme=warehouse|factory|dock|lab|bunker` overrides the scene's default theme. Useful for screenshot tests + A/B playtests.
Custom user-authored themes (in-game editor or external JSON loading). Authored only.
Theme rotation mid-round / per-event. Static per round.
Theme-affects-gameplay (e.g. lab is slipperier). Pure visual.
Day/night cycle within a theme. Static lighting per theme.
Theme-specific VFX (e.g. lab has clean particle sparkles, factory has dirty smoke). Particle palettes COULD adapt slightly via accentEmissive hex but discrete VFX stays uniform across themes.
Theme-specific audio (warehouse-echo, lab-clean). Audio stays the same.
Theme-affected character recipe families. Bomber palette stays bomber-identity, not arena-tinted.
